title: Kubernetes platform hardening
description: Harden the shared Kubernetes platform across network, identity, secrets, and observability controls to meet our internal baseline and reduce blast radius of a compromised workload.

sections.heading: Goals
sections.body: Establish a defense-in-depth posture for the platform: deny-by-default east-west traffic, least-privilege RBAC for both humans and service accounts, encrypted and externally-managed secrets, and tamper-evident audit logging shipped to central storage. Each control should be enforced by policy rather than convention so regressions are caught in CI.

sections.heading: Out of scope
sections.body: Cluster upgrade automation, node OS hardening (CIS benchmarks at the host level), and multi-cluster federation are tracked separately and are not addressed here. Application-level authn/authz inside workloads is the responsibility of the owning teams.

tasks.text: Apply default-deny ingress/egress NetworkPolicy per namespace
Add explicit allow rules for required service dependencies
Verify CNI (Cilium) enforces policies in staging
Audit existing ClusterRoleBindings for wildcard verbs
Replace cluster-admin grants with scoped namespace roles
Add OPA/Gatekeeper constraint blocking privileged role creation
Enable etcd encryption-at-rest with a KMS provider
Migrate static Secrets to External Secrets Operator
Rotate and revoke long-lived credentials found in inventory
Define audit policy covering RBAC and secret access events
Configure apiserver audit log backend to ship to central store
Set retention and immutability on the audit log bucket
Wire alerting on anomalous privileged actions
